newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian government steps into Astra imbroglio.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian government steps into Astra imbroglio.

text.p: The Indonesian government stepped into the imbroglio surrounding the country's largest automobile maker PT Astra International on Wednesday, saying it preferred that the company remain diversely held.
"Astra is better as a public company...(it should) not belong to any one family, or to a certain group," State Secretary Murdiono told reporters.
Brokers said the comments appeared to suggest that the government was opposed to the purchase of a large block of Astra shares by tobacco tycoon Putera Sampoerna.

They said it was significant that a group linked to President Suharto had also evinced interest in Astra, saying the move could have been aimed at blocking a likely takeover of the company by Putera Sampoerna.

The Nusamba Group, 80 percent owned by three cooperatives headed by Suharto, announced earlier this month it was interested in taking up a stake in Astra, just weeks after Putera Sampoerna bought 9.81 percent of the automobile company.
Cigarette firm PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna, headed by Putera Sampoerna, had said a subsidiary had bought an additional 2.85 percent stake in Astra.
The purchases gave Putera Sampoerna effective control over the single-largest holding in the company and there were rumours in the market that he was seeking to increase his stake further.
"At the moment in Astra there is no majority (shareholder)," Murdiono said.
"Once there is a big shareholder, that person can take control," he said, adding that would not be a wise move.
Brokers said the market reacted nervously to the comments.

Astra shares had reached a year-high of 4,600 rupiah ($2.00) in morning trade after the company announced sharply-higher nine-month profit on Tuesday and forecast that its full-year profit would reach 450 billion rupiah against 370.93 billion in 1995.

But shares closed unchanged at 4,250 rupiah as the market was unsure of what would ensue, brokers said. However, volumes were high, with transactions totalling about 30 million shares, or about three percent of the company's equity.
"Too much uncertainty about it. It is better to wait and see the end of the story," said one foreign broker.

"Based on Murdiono's statement, it seems Putera Sampoerna was not allowed to add to his stake in Astra International. Maybe he was even forced to reduce his stake in the firm," said an analyst with a foreign brokerage.
The reference was to an announcement by PT Sampoerna earlier this week that it was looking for a buyer for the 2.85 percent stake held by its subsidiary.

Senior government officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, agreed that Putera Sampoerna could have been persuaded to call off any likely takeover. One said any move to block a takeover "would have been in the public interest".

Astra has the most diversified holdings of any company listed on the Jakarta Stock Exchange. Toyota Motor Co holds 8.26 percent and a range of Indonesian business houses, banks and pension funds hold up to about 10 percent each.
